reviews.review: There's a reason this abomination has seen the memepocalypse as hard as it has. If I 100% this it's because I hate myself.
i gave it an honest try. it's a no. the pew pew shooting is fun enough i guess, but everything else about it is just terrible

It's fun. There is some wacky random bugs here and there. The lack of variety amongst enemies is a little disappointing considering this is an entire galaxy, but overall worth it. Also, the amount of non skippable little cut scenes is really annoying especially when I have to travel between planets/systems. Just let me go, please. final complaint: Why can't I save whenever I want on certain missions or in certain areas? so silly

In short, reeks of very bad writing, deplorable character design and bland/generic gameplay. Nothing really pulls you in and feels special or drives you to keep playing. I felt like I was wasting my time pretty much the entire play session.

After having just played through the Mass Effect Legendary Edition Trilogy and then immedietly hopping to this game afterwards, I will say that this game is subpar in terms of characters and scripting. The only thing I enjoy about this game is the whole "let's colonize another galaxy" premise and the combat system. I like playing the game but it definitely is nowhere near up there with the Trilogy and I honestly think it's hilarious that the Mass Effect Milky Way galaxy has at least a dozen sapient alien races and Andromeda has maybe two and a half, making Andromeda as an alien galaxy more barebones than the Milky Way. You're sending several council races through deep space to another Galaxy just for the two dominant races in Andromeda to be two dimensional compared to the likes of the Turians or the Salarians. I would rate this game at least a 6/10 solely because it's enjoyable ENOUGH to keep playing and the game loses a point solely because there are no Quarians and the Quarian ark ship remains in DLC hell.
